manifest.description: Define your terms once. The first time each one appears on a page it gets a small, accessible tooltip with its definition, reachable by mouse, touch and keyboard. Headings, links and code are left alone.
manifest.name: Glossary Tooltips

panels.description: Terms and their definitions. The first time a term appears on a page it is underlined and shows its definition on hover, tap or keyboard focus. Changes apply to a page the next time it is published.

fields.description: Turn this off to leave every page exactly as it was rendered.
fields.name: enabled
fields.title: Show glossary tooltips

fields.description: One per line: the term, a colon, then its definition. For example: SEO: Search engine optimisation, making pages easy to find. Add spellings with a vertical bar, like API | APIs: ... Lines starting with # are ignored.
fields.name: terms
fields.title: Terms

fields.description: Match case exactly. Off, "api" in your list also matches "API" on a page.
fields.name: match-case
fields.title: Match case

fields.description: The underline or highlight. Leave empty for amber (#ca8a04).
fields.name: color
fields.title: Colour

fields.description: Slugs, separated by commas, that never get tooltips. For example: home, contact
fields.name: exclude
fields.title: Pages to skip

panels.title: Glossary tooltips

store.tagline: Explain jargon in place: a tooltip on the first use of each term.
store.longDescription:
Glossary Tooltips lets you explain the words your readers might not know, right where they meet them. List your terms and a one-line definition for each in the site settings. The first time a term appears on a page it gets a subtle dotted underline, and hovering, tapping or tabbing to it shows the definition in a small tooltip. Later mentions stay plain, so pages never fill up with underlines.

It stays out of the way. Headings, links, code, buttons, forms, navigation, headers and footers are never touched, matching is whole-word, and the longest term wins when two overlap. Add other spellings with a vertical bar, such as API | APIs, and choose whether case matters. Anything you want left alone can be marked with data-glossary="off".

It is accessible by default. Each term is a real button inside a dfn element, described by a tooltip, so keyboard and screen reader users get the definition too. Escape dismisses it, the pointer can move onto it without it vanishing, it stays inside the screen on phones, it respects reduced motion and it is hidden when printing.

It is light: one small stylesheet and about 1 KB of inline script, added only to pages that actually contain a term. No fonts, images or third-party requests. Pick a dotted underline or a soft highlight in your own colour; amber is the default.

The only permission it asks for is storage, to keep your terms. Refuse it and pages are left exactly as they were.

screenshots.caption: The first mention of each term gets a dotted underline; hover shows its definition.
Keyboard friendly: tab to a term and its tooltip opens, with a clear focus ring.
The soft highlight look in your own colour. Tooltips stay inside the screen.
Settings: one term per line, match case, look, colour and pages to skip.
